name: AlexNet ImageNet image classification
description: A deep convolutional neural network trained using GPUs for large-scale image classification, evaluated in the ImageNet challenge.

date.basis: Date or approximate interval stated by the source for this event.

events.statement: Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton published ImageNet classification experiments with a deep convolutional network.
events.scope: Reported ImageNet competition experiment, not general visual understanding.

evidence.supports: Paper specifies authors, GPU network and 2012 contest result.

date.label: 20 March 2025
date.basis: Museum publication date for release announcement.

events.statement: Computer History Museum and Google made the historical AlexNet source code available as open source.
events.caveats: The 2012 paper had already made a GPU implementation publicly available; this release concerns the historical source archive and does not establish its first public access.

evidence.supports: Museum describes the release and Google’s role.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated event established in the cited sources for this scoped record; it does not assert global priority.

places.note: Paper gives University of Toronto affiliations.

measures.subject: Authors’ variant in ILSVRC-2012 test competition
measures.conditions: Top-five test error in the cited competition; not top-one accuracy or a general measure of real-world vision.

evidence.supports: The authors report 15.3% top-five error for their 2012 competition variant.

caveats: Convolutional neural networks and GPU use predated this study; performance depends on dataset, evaluation and model variant.

research.note: Source-backed initial research; independent review is pending. Independent review checked the 2012 paper, its public cuda-convnet footnote and 15.3% contest variant, plus the CHM release and CUDA implementation account.

links.statement: The reported 2012 implementation extended CUDA-written cuda-convnet to train the ImageNet network on GPUs.
links.caveats: This applies to the authors’ implementation and historical experiment, not a claim that the abstract network architecture can only run on CUDA.

evidence.supports: Museum curator identifies the original CUDA code and its extension for ImageNet.
The authors identify their publicly available GPU implementation as cuda-convnet.
